sources.entry: Petrichor - Offline music player with broad format support, lyrics, playlists, and queue management. [![Open-Source Software][OSS Icon]](https://github.com/kushalpandya/Petrichor) ![Freeware][Freeware Icon]
Petrichor - Offline music player for macOS with library management, smart playlists, synced lyrics and an equalizer.

summary.one_liner: Petrichor is an offline music player for macOS 14+ that manages a local library, plays dozens of audio formats, and offers playlists, synced lyrics, internet radio, and an equalizer.
summary.what_it_does: Petrichor scans user-added music folders, reads metadata, and stores library data in a SQLite database with FTS5 search. It plays over 40 audio formats (the README lists 46 file extensions), including lossless types such as FLAC, ALAC, WAV, and APE, plus DSD and common lossy formats. Users can create, import, and export playlists, including smart playlists with conditional, negative, and regular-expression rules, and can manage the play queue by drag and drop. Additional features include synced lyrics with download of missing lyrics, Internet Radio streaming, gapless playback, crossfade, ReplayGain, an equalizer, AirPlay 2 output, and Last.fm scrobbling. Network features such as lyrics, artist bios, radio, and scrobbling are disabled by default according to the README.
use_cases: Play a large local music collection on a Mac offline
Organize and browse MP3, FLAC, ALAC and other audio files by folder or library view
Create smart playlists based on rules
Listen to synced lyrics while playing music
Stream internet radio stations and save them in collections
Play music with AirPlay 2 or the equalizer on macOS
how_to_run: Download the latest .dmg from the Releases page
Open the .dmg and drag Petrichor into the Applications folder
In Applications, right-click Petrichor and choose Open
Or install with Homebrew: brew install --cask petrichor
notable: Smart playlists with conditional, negative, and regular-expression rules
Playback and metadata reading via CrescendoKit, built on FFmpeg and TagLib
Sandboxed and notarized by Apple, and does not modify audio files or folder structure
Menubar and dock playback controls, plus Shortcuts and Siri automation support
Pins almost any item to the sidebar and supports a folder view
caveats: Requires macOS 14 or later; no Windows or Linux support is mentioned
The playback engine and metadata reader (CrescendoKit) are proprietary binary distributions, not open source
Building from source needs Xcode, and building a notarized .dmg requires a paid Apple Developer account (a --bypass-notary option exists)
Tracker modules (MOD, IT, S3M, XM), DRM-protected files, audiobooks (.m4b), RealAudio, and MIDI are not supported; tracker formats were dropped in 1.7
